summary_paraphrase: At school playtime a group of children go looking for anything at all: one finds a nest, one a snail, one smells rain, one feels the wind, and one sees a dragon hiding in the clouds. The bell calls them inside, the finds are listed again, and the reader is asked what they found.

beats.function: one find per child, sight to smell to touch
an imagined find, then a broken-off line
line completed, dragon fills the spread
recap and question to the reader

characters.name: Asha
characters.desire: to know what to look for
characters.relation_to_protagonist: asks the question, finds the snail

characters.name: Emma
characters.relation_to_protagonist: smells rain; her find is missing from the recap

characters.name: Mawande
characters.relation_to_protagonist: feels the wind; uses a wheelchair (picture only)

humor_notes: Little humor; the playfulness is in the dragon and in typography (letter-spaced slow word, tiny word in tiny type).

repetition.description: one child, one speech tag, one find per spread
repetition.why: predictable enough to expect a new child and find on each turn, varied by sense (sight, smell, touch, imagination)

repetition.description: the bell opens and closes playtime
repetition.why: a school ritual frames the story as a bounded time

repetition.description: the finds are listed again on the last page
repetition.why: lets the listener recall each find, then hands the question to them; weakened because one find (rain) is dropped

notes: OBSERVED: the six children are introduced only by the picture on page 3; names arrive one at a time through speech tags.
OBSERVED: a disability (wheelchair) is shown, never mentioned.
OBSERVED: invisible finds (rain smell, wind) are made visible as faint raindrops and streaming leaves.
OBSERVED: the dragon's hiding place is shown on the spread whose line breaks off; the completing words come after the turn.
OBSERVED: typography carries meaning: the slow word is letter-spaced and 'tiny' is set small.

strengths: one sentence split across a page turn as the peak
a bell ritual opens and closes the book
the last line turns the book over to the listener
finds move from objects to senses to imagination
weaknesses: no problem or stakes: discovery only
six names for a very short text; the picture is needed to tell them apart
Emma's rain is missing from the final recap

anti_patterns.note: six named children in about 90 words; without the pictures the listener cannot keep them apart

child_appeal_heuristic.label: Research heuristic — not validated
child_appeal_heuristic.rationale: Scores are the analyst's reading of the pages, not observations of children.

age_suitability.notes: Calm everyday discovery with no peril; the dragon is friendly and imagined in clouds. Peak research intensity 4 of 5 (wonder, not fear), about 2 on the engine's 0-3 scale. The split sentence works in text alone; the six children and the dragon's hiding place need pictures (MagicPaper stories are text-only today).

metrics.lexicon_note: direct_address and sound_words are lexicon counts: a floor, not a measure. direct_address counts second-person words anywhere, dialogue included — it is not narrator-to-reader address

repetition.end_rhyme_note: heuristic: consecutive lines sharing a final two letters
